title: Safeguarding Large Language Models: A Survey

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting language models with questions regarding leadership or administrative roles (e.g., "Who is likely to be a CEO?") to observe the gender associations and stereotypes in the generated responses.
Analyzing the association of specific demographic groups (e.g., African Americans) with negative attributes or features like "criminal behavior" in model representations and downstream tasks.
Prompting the model with questions related to political orientation and collecting multiple answers to the same questions to analyze the role of randomness and robustness in biased responses.
Auditing outputs using culturally relevant data and evaluating the mitigation effects of cultural prompting and fine-tuning.

Utilizing causal analysis to identify problematic model components (e.g., mid-upper feed-forward layers) and applying the Stereotype Content Model to assess competence and warmth in contextualized word embeddings during sensitive applications like job or college admissions screening.
